newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle close lower but above lows.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle close lower but above lows.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed lower on technical pressure and cash market concerns, but values finished off the day's lows, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.450 to 0.025 cent per lb lower paced by April at 65.450 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.400 0.650 cent lower with March off 0.500 at 68.475 cents.

Technical pressure was evident from the start in both pits. Monday's sharp break and lower close after new contract highs were posted in distant months of live cattle and all months of feeders after the Cattle Inventory report rally, turned charts down, traders said.

Pressure in live cattle also stemmed from wholesale beef sales and the fact that packers refused to budge from $62 to $63 per cwt bids for fed cattle. However, rolling of short positions into April limited February's loss, they said.
"Near-term (fed) cattle supplies are more than adequate," one trader said.
After the close, fed cattle traded $1 per cwt lower at $63 in the Texas-Oklahoma panhandle area and Kansas.
Selling by R.J. O'Brien and Refco offset buying by E.D.&F. Man in April and touched off sell stops early, sources said.
In live cattle options, commercials sold June 64 and 66 calls and bought April 68 and 70 calls. April risk reversals, buying of 64 calls and selling of 68 calls, were noted, traders added.

Feeder cattle futures were also depressed by higher corn futures and talk that more feeders will be sent to auction early next week. One trader noted reports that 20,000 head of feeders will Oklahoma City on Monday next week, likely due to increased movement of feeders off of winter pastures, he said.
USDA reported feeder cattle receipts at the Oklahoma City auction Monday at 12,000 head and 13,427 on Monday a week earlier.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.60 at $70.05 per cwt, but provided only little support early, they said.

R.J. O'Brien sold March while Rosenthal Collins, Refco and Cargill Investor Services sold April. ING and ADM Investor Services bought March and Cargill spread long April feeders/short August live cattle, pit sources said.
